entities.description: The suit of Hearts in a standard playing card deck. Corresponds to the tarot suit of Cups and the element of Water. Associated with love, emotion, relationships, intuition, and domestic life. In cartomancy Hearts are the most positive suit, relating to feelings, home, and happiness.

The suit of Diamonds in a standard playing card deck. Corresponds to the tarot suit of Pentacles (Coins) and the element of Earth. Associated with money, material matters, business, practical affairs, and earthly concerns. In cartomancy Diamonds represent financial matters and material opportunities.

The suit of Clubs in a standard playing card deck. Corresponds to the tarot suit of Wands and the element of Fire. Associated with energy, ambition, career, creativity, and enterprise. The club symbol derives from the trefoil clover (trèfle in French). In cartomancy Clubs represent work, passion, and dynamic activity.

The suit of Spades in a standard playing card deck. Corresponds to the tarot suit of Swords and the element of Air. The name derives from the Spanish espada (sword). Associated with challenges, conflict, intellect, truth, and difficult transformations. In cartomancy Spades represent obstacles, change, and difficult but clarifying truths.
The highest-ranking card in Spades. Traditionally known as the Death Card in playing card divination. Associated with transformation, endings, and authority.

extendedData.meaning: death, transformation, and the ending that clears the way for something new
